definitions.meaning: To be becoming or fit, to behove

sub_senses.heading: chiefly used impersonally, it behoves, it is becoming or fit, ought

quotations.old_english: Ic axige hwæðer hit mihte gedafnian Abrahame
quotations.english: I will ask whether it was becoming to Abraham

quotations.old_english: Láreówum gedafenaþ ðæt hí mid wísdómes sealte geleáffulra manna mód sylton
quotations.english: it befits teachers that they salt the minds of believing men with the salt of wisdom

quotations.citations: Ps. Th. 64, 1 : 92, 7 : Ælfc. Gr. 33; Som. 37, 20 : Andr. Kmbl. 633; An. 317

quotations.old_english: Me gedafenaþ óðrum ceastrum Godes ríce bodian
quotations.latin: aliis civitātibus oportet me evangelizāre regnum Dei

quotations.old_english: Hit gedafnode ðæt se Ælmihtiga ǽrest ðæt hwílendlíce leóht geworhte
quotations.english: it was becoming that the Almighty first created the temporary light

source_text: ge-dafenian, -dafnian, -dæfnia; p. ode; pp. od To be becoming or fit, to behove; decere, conv&e-short;n&i-long;re : chiefly used impersonally, it behoves, it is becoming or fit, ought; d&e-short;cet, oportet :-- Ic axige hwæðer hit mihte gedafnian Abrahame I will ask whether it was becoming to Abraham, Boutr. Scrd. 21, 47. Láreówum gedafenaþ ðæt hí mid wísdómes sealte geleáffulra manna mód sylton it befits teachers that they salt the minds of believing men with the salt of wisdom, Homl. Th. ii. 536, 16 : L. E. I. 24; Th. ii. 420, 32. Me gedæfnaþ me oportet, Jn. Skt. Lind. 9, 4. Ðé gedæfneþ te oportet, 3, 7. Ðé gedafenaþ te d&e-short;cet, Ps. Th. 64, 1 : 92, 7 : Ælfc. Gr. 33; Som. 37, 20 : Andr. Kmbl. 633; An. 317. Me gedafenaþ óðrum ceastrum Godes ríce bodian aliis civit&a-long;t&i-short;bus oportet me evangeliz&a-long;re regnum Dei, Lk. Bos. 4, 43 : Ælfc. Gr. 33; Som. 37, 21. Gedafenode d&e-short;cuit, 33; Som. 37, 21 : Bd. 4, 11; S. 579. 11. Hit gedafnode ðæt se Ælmihtiga ǽrest ðæt hwílendlíce leóht geworhte it was becoming that the Almighty first created the temporary light, Boutr. Scrd. 19, 4 : 21, 39. Gedæfnad is ús decet nos, Mt. Kmbl. Lind. 3, 15.
